source_evidence: Regular investing means that you put a set dollar amount or a set percentage of your income into your investment accounts.
question: Misconception: Regular investing only counts if you contribute a large amount each time. Is that true?
answer: No. Regular investing can mean contributing a set dollar amount or a set percentage of your income. The source also explains that starting earlier gives compounding more time to work; it does not say that contributions must be large to count.
